clue.text: Furious English master who's out for a duck?

parts.note: furious means wild with rage
H. W. Fowler, author of Modern English Usage, is the classic master of English style

explanation.surface: An angry English schoolmaster gets dismissed without scoring at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out for a duck' suggests a cricketer dismissed for nought; here it means someone out hunting ducks.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunter of wild birds such as ducks goes out shooting them, which is literally being out for a duck.

clue.text: Spoken request for identification of this tree?

definitions.text: Spoken request for identification of this tree?

indicators.note: spoken says the question is heard, not written, giving a word of similar sound

parts.words: request for identification of this tree
parts.note: asking which of the elm trees it is

explanation.surface: Someone asks out loud what kind of tree this is.
explanation.definitionFit: The wych elm is a native British elm species, so it is a tree.

clue.text: Profitable development of vital cure

indicators.note: a development is a working out into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Developing an essential remedy can make a lot of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that brings in plenty of money is money-making.

clue.text: Suffer a blow and be short of cash

explanation.surface: Taking a hit and being broke at the same time.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'blow' is a gust of cold air here; to feel the pinch for money is a British idiom with the same wording.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold current of air blowing on you is a literal blow; the idiom means to suffer financial hardship.

clue.text: See jokers holding up nurse

indicators.note: holding means the jokers' word contains another piece

parts.note: wits are jokers

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the nurse's letters read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: SEN is a State Enrolled Nurse

explanation.surface: Watch the comedians delaying a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding up' does two jobs: 'holding' is the container signal and 'up' turns the nurse upwards, as this is a down clue. SEN, State Enrolled Nurse, is an old British nursing grade.
explanation.definitionFit: To witness something is to observe it happen.

clue.text: English men dispossessed by law.

annotationWithheld.why: English men dispossessed by law. (7): E (English) plus nothing that 'men' gives makes VICTED; no parse found for the rest of EVICTED

clue.text: A man's device for focusing light

explanation.surface: Some man's gadget for concentrating light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A man's' read as Len's, belonging to a man called Len, spells the answer exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved piece of glass in a camera or spectacles brings light rays to a focus.

clue.text: Former priest upset deportee

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down clue the priest's letters run backwards

parts.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: An ex-priest is distressed at being deported.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone banished from their homeland is a deported person.

clue.text: Prominent stranger seen in street

indicators.note: in shows the stranger goes inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: an alien is a stranger or foreigner

explanation.surface: A conspicuous outsider is spotted in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A salient feature is one that stands out noticeably.

clue.text: Stubborn officer: commanding many in inauspicious situation:

indicators.note: in shows the officer and many go inside the inauspicious situation

parts.note: an unpromising situation is an inauspicious one
CO is the commanding officer
M, the Roman thousand, stands for many

explanation.surface: An obstinate officer leads a great many men in a bleak position.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusing to make concessions means being inflexible.

clue.text: Vehicle for revolution

explanation.surface: A car designed for a political uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A bicycle is a vehicle, and one complete turn or rotation is a revolution.

clue.text: Regularly occurring test containing nine parts

indicators.note: containing tells us the word for test holds another piece inside it

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: parts, as a verb, breaks up the word nine so its letters come apart and regroup

explanation.surface: A recurring exam made up of nine sections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like a noun for sections, but works as a verb that breaks the number apart, giving ENNI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening every three years recurs at a fixed regular interval.

clue.text: Bill's passing is producing dramatic scenes

explanation.surface: Getting a parliamentary bill through is a theatrical business.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill's passing into law is its legislation, and acting out scenes on stage is performing them.

clue.text: Neat view of the plant

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
an eye is a view or way of looking

explanation.surface: A tidy outlook on some vegetation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy, but it is the archaic word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The ox-eye daisy is a familiar wild flower, so this names a plant species.

clue.text: First and second misses

parts.note: misses as young unmarried women; and in cricket, overs with no runs scored, also called after a first or untried thing

explanation.surface: Two failed attempts in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as two failures; the clue means young unmarried women, with a nod to maiden as 'first' (a maiden voyage).
explanation.definitionFit: Unmarried young women were once addressed as Miss, and a maiden voyage or speech is the first one.

clue.text: Security system, installed originally in regimental HQ

indicators.note: in tells us the opening letters go inside the word for regimental HQ

parts.note: a depot is a regiment's headquarters

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of each of the words system and installed

explanation.surface: An alarm system has been fitted at the regiment's base.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid down as a pledge or guarantee serves as security against loss.

clue.text: Stockbrokers initially embezzle to play the market

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of Stockbrokers

parts.note: to peculate is to embezzle

explanation.surface: Stockbrokers start by stealing funds to gamble with on the exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: Trading in shares hoping for a profit from price moves is speculation.

clue.text: Successful bounder, comparatively innocent

explanation.surface: A rogue who prospers is, by comparison, rather harmless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' looks like a cad, but here it is a jumper, and a successful one gets over the fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that gets over a fence is one that jumps it cleanly; more free of guilt means less blameworthy.

clue.text: One demonstrating approval for a striker

explanation.surface: A fan cheering a footballer who scores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' looks like a footballer; it is the tongue of a bell that hits it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone applauding shows approval; the tongue inside a bell strikes it.

clue.text: Soak last of 19 in port for this dish

indicators.note: in shows the soak and the final letter go inside the port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a port
a soak is a drunkard, a sot

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the answer to 19

explanation.surface: A drunk in harbour drinks the last of something with his meal.
explanation.walkthrough: '19' is 19 down, APRICOT, whose last letter is T.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian rice dish cooked in stock is a meal served on a plate.

clue.text: Birds resorting to caves

indicators.note: read as re-sorting, these letters are sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: Birds taking refuge in caves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resorting' looks like going to a refuge, but read as re-sorting it rearranges TO CAVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Avocets are wading birds with upturned bills, so the plural names birds.

clue.text: Fruit found in simple dwelling after almost a month

indicators.note: after places the dwelling behind the shortened month
almost means the month loses its final letter

parts.note: April is a month
a cot is a small simple cottage

explanation.surface: Fruit discovered in a humble cottage near the end of a month.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is an orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Unproductive set stirred up anger

indicators.note: stirred up means the letters of set are mixed

parts.note: to rile is to anger

explanation.surface: An idle group got everyone worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren land or a barren effort yields nothing.

clue.text: Farewell to the French about to depart

definitions.text: Farewell to the French about to depart

parts.words: Farewell to the French about to depart
parts.note: the parting word a French speaker says when leaving, literally commending the hearer to God

explanation.surface: Saying goodbye to the French as one prepares to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: This French leave-taking word, used in English too, means goodbye for a long time or for ever.

clue.text: Clubs in which naughty sailors may be found

definitions.text: in which naughty sailors may be found

explanation.surface: Nightclubs where badly behaved sailors hang out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' looks like nightclubs; they are golf clubs. Sailors punished were put 'in irons', shackles.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers use iron-headed clubs; shackles are fetters that hold offenders.

clue.text: Make free with divesture of chains

indicators.note: to make free with something is to take liberties with it, so these letters are freely rearranged

explanation.surface: Liberation by casting off one's chains.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests release from chains, but 'chains' is the definition and DIVESTURE is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Being held in bondage is slavery, figuratively being in chains.

clue.text: Forward-looking governor put in to hold up movement out of control

indicators.note: put in says the governor's letters are placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: to prop is to hold up
a tic is an involuntary twitch
HE, His Excellency, is the title of a colonial governor

explanation.surface: A visionary governor is installed to stop an anarchic political movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement out of control' looks political; it is a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Predicting what will come means looking ahead, like a seer.

clue.text: Asian king joining a queen in the islands

indicators.note: in shows the king, a and queen go inside the letters for the islands

parts.note: I is an abbreviation for island, so two of them are II
R, for rex, is king
Q is the abbreviation for queen in chess and cards

explanation.surface: A king from Asia joins a queen on some islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq is in western Asia, so its native is an Asian.

clue.text: Career that was of little value

explanation.surface: A job that turned out to be worth little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' is the verb, to charge headlong; 'not worth a rush' means worthless, the rush being a reed.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to dash headlong; a reed of trifling worth gave the idiom for something worthless.

clue.text: Like Vasco da Gama describing a man-of-war?

explanation.surface: A comparison of the explorer Vasco da Gama with a warship.
explanation.walkthrough: A man-of-war looks like a warship; here it is the jellyfish-like Portuguese man-of-war.
explanation.definitionFit: Vasco da Gama was a navigator from Lisbon, and the stinging sea creature is named after that nation.
